conventions.convention: Euclidean state coordinates are dimensionless numerical values obtained by dividing quantities by their displayed SI units. Energy and transfers use joules, volume cubic metres, and species amounts moles.

A frame is a Galilean coordinate chart. Internal energy is evaluated in a statewise instantaneous center-of-mass rest chart; process bookkeeping selects one fixed inertial chart. A single rest chart works throughout an interval exactly when the center-of-mass velocity is constant.

Equilibrium is a primitive model designation. Positive-mole state charts exclude absent-species zero coordinates. Designated fixed-composition slices are nonempty, open and convex; these properties are not asserted for every full state domain.

Process records have equilibrium endpoints but no imposed continuity or differentiability of their configuration curves. Q and W_on are process functionals defined on the core closed-record class, with positive values meaning heat entering and work done on the system. Adiabatic means Q[P]=0.

The core closed-record class requires positive supplied mass, endpoint center-of-mass velocities, and zero endpoint changes in separately tracked translational kinetic and external-field potential energy.

Bulk composition applies only to admitted separated pairs and omits cross-interface and long-range interaction energy. Scaling uses positive dimensionless factors, possibly restricted domains, and distinct scaled-system tags; it does not identify the scaled constitutive law with the original law or postulate entropy scaling.
Transfers across the compound's outer boundary are external; transfers between its subsystems are internal. Closed excludes matter transfer, and isolated excludes both matter and energy transfer.

load_bearing.statement: Admitted records are typed tuples with equilibrium endpoints and a model-declared configuration curve. The core closed-record class imposes zero changes in center-of-mass kinetic and external-field potential energy; Q,W_on: P_cl(s)→R are signed process functionals, and adiabatic means Q[P]=0.

The representation map π_c:E_c→R^(r+2) assigns unique dimensionless numerical coordinates (U,V,n_1,…,n_r), with V>0 and every n_j>0; D_c is its image. Each designated fixed-composition slice Γ_c,n is a specified nonempty open convex subset of R².

Allowed chart changes are t′=t+τ and x′=Rx+a−bt with RᵀR=I₃. Admitted mechanical models supply compatible center-of-mass data. U is recorded in a statewise instantaneous rest chart and excludes bulk translational kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energy.

For every admitted separated pair, a composition map into the declared compound state domain adds internal energy, volume and aligned species amounts. For admitted scaled copies, δ_λ(x)=λx maps B_c,λ into D_c^(λ), retaining the distinct material tag.
For every admitted core closed record with equilibrium endpoints, fixed material constitution and the stated zero-change exclusions, U_c(x_P^+)−U_c(x_P^-)=Q[P]+W_on[P].
The framework uses SI quantities and dimensionless numerical coordinate representatives; J=kg·m²·s⁻², N=kg·m·s⁻² and Pa=J·m⁻³. State and transfer meanings are supplied separately from their units.

A system has a model-selected outer boundary and declared permitted transfer channels; subsystem transfers are internal to a compound. Closed systems exclude matter transfer, and isolated systems exclude matter and energy transfer.

concerns.concern: The definition says, “A system is open when only the named matter species and other named transfer channels may cross its boundary.” It does not explicitly require any permitted matter-transfer channel. With an empty permitted species set, that condition also describes a closed system. Clarify whether these classifications intentionally overlap or whether open requires a matter-transfer permission.

alerts.finding: The Definition quantifies over “P∈P_s” and requires “Q[P]=0”. Its cited supplier def-td-process-and-protocol defines Q,W_on only on P_cl(s), a restricted subset requiring closure and zero kinetic/external-energy changes. No extension of Q to P_s is supplied. Thus the accessibility predicate evaluates a function outside its declared domain and does not define a relation on the stated witness class.

seams_checked.note: Checked the consuming uses against the framework interfaces. State domains retain their local chart qualifications; contact protocols supply additional constituent endpoint maps; entropy additivity and homogeneity are separately adopted rather than inferred from coordinate additivity. The common-law branch explicitly adds the transport needed for same-function homogeneity. Closed second-law records preserve the kinetic/external-energy restrictions. The framework page reserves entropy and equilibrium principles for later pages.

Tagged scaling, fixed-composition slice embeddings, SI energy meaning and additional channel-model assumptions are distinguished appropriately. However, def-td-adiabatic-accessibility uses Q[P] for P∈P_s while the framework defines Q only on P_cl(s); the alert records the exact domain mismatch. The framework supplies no reverse extension or broader transfer-map interface that closes it.
